programme: No shared module can be named from this list. TEAD4 (Hippo effector), SOX9 (progenitor/chondro-epithelial TF) and TBX2 (senescence-bypass TF) each have real, independent traction in bladder cancer, but they do not converge on one documented complex or pathway together, and none of GATA6, PITX2, SATB2, NFIA, TBX2, SOX9, ZNF410, ZBTB18, MAFF, IRF2BPL or PER2 is placed in IBS by anything retrieved except PER2, whose IBS role (intestinal barrier/gut-brain signalling) is mechanistically unrelated to its one bladder-cancer citation (circadian control of heme/porphyrin synthesis used diagnostically in tumours). Forcing these twelve into a single story would mean treating 'developmental transcription factor' as the mechanism, which is the same move the instructions warn against for 'immune response.'
role_in_a: TEAD4, TBX2 and SOX9 have direct literature support as drivers of proliferation, EMT and senescence bypass in bladder cancer (PMID 35581606, 40301305, 39934701, 41653270 for TEAD4; PMID 25394776, 29367430, 30089113 for TBX2; PMID 23628807, 32605249 for SOX9), but these act as separate lines of evidence, not one pathway.
role_in_b: Essentially undocumented here. Only PER2 has a genuine IBS-relevant citation (PMID 40847793, intestinal epithelial Per2 and gut-brain/depression signalling); SATB2's IBS-adjacent hits are colon-organoid differentiation methods papers (PMID 39716027, 28648364), not IBS studies; GATA6, PITX2, NFIA, TBX2, SOX9, ZNF410, ZBTB18, MAFF, IRF2BPL return no IBS evidence at all.
shared_axis: None can be written honestly. The candidate link (PER2 as a circadian node present in both tissues) fails because the two cited roles of PER2 are different biology in different compartments (tumour heme metabolism vs. gut epithelial permeability), not one axis operating in both diseases.
reasoning: The factor list mixes an oncogenic effector (TEAD4), lineage/developmental TFs from unrelated canonical tissues (GATA6-foregut, PITX2-laterality/craniofacial, SATB2-osteoblast/colorectal, SOX9-chondro/gonad/gut, TBX2-limb/melanocyte, NFIA-glia/lung), a clock gene (PER2), a stress-responsive bZIP (MAFF) and three near-silent zinc fingers (ZNF410, ZBTB18, IRF2BPL). Even discarding the discordant ones (GATA6, TBX2, SATB2), what remains does not cohere into a nameable complex, and the record itself states IBS evidence is absent or unclear for nearly every factor — that asymmetry is a fact about the query, not evidence the story is a novel one, so it cannot be upgraded to 'unexpected.'
support: PMID 35581606, 40301305, 39934701, 41653270 — TEAD4 in bladder cancer via YAP/TAZ-TEAD-driven proliferation/EMT, unrelated to IBS. PMID 25394776, 29367430, 30089113 — TBX2 methylation/expression as a bladder-cancer prognostic marker, no IBS link. PMID 23628807, 32605249 — SOX9 in bladder-cancer methylation/retinoid biology, no IBS link. PMID 32219034 — NFI family (incl. NFIA) reviewed across human cancers, bladder cancer relevance uncertain from abstract. PMID 39798644 — PITX2 in developing bladder/urethra compartments, developmental not disease evidence, no IBS link. PMID 34801602 — SATB2-positive secondary malignancy after bowel-segment urologic reconstruction, a surgical/iatrogenic context, not spontaneous bladder cancer or IBS. PMID 39716027, 28648364 — SATB2 in colon-organoid differentiation methods, tissue-relevant to IBS but not an IBS study. PMID 39682298 — PER2 and circadian porphyrin/heme accumulation in bladder cancer, no IBS relevance. PMID 40847793 — PER2 in intestinal epithelium and depression via gut-brain signalling, the only genuine IBS-relevant citation in the set.
how_to_falsify: Take the three factors with the strongest independent bladder-cancer evidence (TEAD4, TBX2, SOX9) and ask whether they co-bind or co-regulate any shared target set in colonic/IBS-relevant tissue (e.g. ChIP-seq or CUT&RUN in colonic epithelial organoids, or public ENCODE/ReMap colon data): if their bladder-cancer target genes (VEGFA/HIF1A/FGFR1 for TEAD4, MITF/CDKN2A/MYCN for TBX2, COL2A1/COL9A1/CDH2 for SOX9) show no shared occupancy or co-expression module in gut tissue, that is direct evidence against any common programme, matching the incoherent verdict reached here.
caveats: 100 patient-group comparisons behind a single independent cohort pair means the recurrence counts (51-75/100) reflect one underlying dataset resampled many ways, not 100 independent replications — treat the 'supported_in' fractions as one study's internal robustness, not external confirmation. Bladder (urothelial) and colorectal (IBS-relevant) tissue are anatomically adjacent via the embryonic cloaca, which is exactly why shared developmental TFs (GATA6, PITX2, SATB2, TBX2, SOX9) are easy to over-read as a 'module' when they may simply reflect that both tissues are hindgut/urogenital-sinus derivatives expressing overlapping lineage TFs without a functional module linking the two diseases. GATA6, TBX2 and SATB2 are marked discordant, meaning even their direction of regulation differs between the two disease networks, which argues against treating them as a shared axis rather than for it. The single-view exclusions (POU4F2, NFE2L3, FHL2, BCL6B, DBP, PAX7, SHOX2, KAT6A, CBFA2T3, ARID3A, FOXK2, ZNF287) and tissue-generic exclusions are not available in this material, so it cannot be confirmed whether any obvious master regulator was correctly filtered out before this list was built.
